title: Spec Project Configuration
description: One file at .spec/project.json. Covers project meta, area index, code-repo paths (config-driven, not submodules), project-level architecture defaults inherited by every area, deployment topology, and Apalache settings. Per-dev state (path overrides, active change last_change) goes in .spec/local.json (gitignored). Units of work are change manifests in specs/changes/ (change.schema.json).

areas.description: Index of all spec files under specs/. Each entry names where the area JSON lives, the kind, and the code mapping (if any).

name.description: Area slug. File is specs/<name>.area.json (or .contract.json per kind).

kind.description: 'ui' is a deprecated alias for area-with-screens; use 'area'.

repos.description: Code repositories the project's areas live in. Logical name → repo metadata. Local paths come from .spec/local.json (gitignored).

url.description: Clone URL; informational — shown when a repo checkout is missing from .spec/local.json.

architecture.description: Project-wide architecture defaults. Each area inherits these unless its `architecture.inherits_project` is false. Same shape as area.architecture (minus components, which are per-area).

topology.description: Deployment topology (Layer 4). Components are <area>.<component> from area JSON files.

quint.description: OPTIONAL. Tunes the two quint accelerations spec-record runs around the Apalache path — the advisory `quint run` pre-gate and the batched `quint verify --invariants` green path — plus the backend properties[] are checked on. Every field has a working default; the block absent means defaults. Nothing here can produce a verification verdict.

eval_backend.description: Evaluator for `quint run` / `quint test`. Rust is the fast one. spec-record probes `quint run --help` first, so an older quint without --backend runs its own default rather than failing on an unknown flag.

max_samples.description: How many randomized executions the pre-gate explores. Also the denominator of the witness pre-screen's 'N of M traces'.

max_steps.description: Step bound for the simulator. Defaults to apalache.max_steps, so the pre-gate explores the depth the model checker will.

seed.description: Fixes the simulator's random choices. Set it when a pre-gate finding has to be reproducible; leave it out for fresh exploration every run.

simulate_timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock cap on the pre-gate. Short on purpose — its whole value is being cheap relative to the model checker.

batch_invariants.description: Try every bounded invariant in one `quint verify --invariants` run before falling back to one run per id. A clean batch records the same verdicts for one Apalache start instead of N; a batch that is not clean changes nothing, because every id then takes the per-id path and gets its own trace.

temporal_backend.description: Backend for properties[] (liveness), which run as `quint verify --temporal=<name>`. TLC by default because Apalache's temporal support is partial. TLC is explicit-state: no --max-steps bound and no ITF trace, so a temporal counterexample is recorded without one.

z3.description: OPTIONAL SMT backend. Present only when some invariant declares proof: "smt". Absent = the backend is off and nothing about the existing paths changes.

binary.description: Path to the z3 executable. Overridden per-developer by Z3_BIN in the environment; falls back to whatever `z3` is on PATH.

alloy.description: OPTIONAL structural backend. Present only when some area declares formal_model.alloy_file. Absent = Alloy is off and nothing about the existing Apalache path changes. Requires Alloy 6.2+ (its CLI was introduced there) and the same JVM 17+ Apalache already needs.

jar_path.description: Path to org.alloytools.alloy.dist.jar. Overridden per-developer by ALLOY_JAR in the environment, which is where a machine-specific path belongs.

solver.description: SAT solver id passed to `alloy exec -s`. Pinned because a scope-bounded verdict is only reproducible against a named solver; sat4j is the pure-Java default and needs no native library.

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock cap enforced by spec-record. The Alloy CLI has no timeout flag of its own.
